question: Should execution results redact secret-shaped output by default only when they also carry a stable machine-readable redaction signal, or should raw output remain available until a reveal-and-marker contract is designed?
rationale: The patch closes a real secret-exposure boundary but also expands the documented risk of agents persisting masked values; choosing the permanent output and reveal contract requires security and product intent.

options.title: Redact with explicit signal
options.body: Keep default redaction, add stable structured metadata plus a text warning, and defer any privileged raw reveal path to separate reviewed work.

options.title: Accept implicit redaction
options.body: Merge the current behavior while explicitly accepting byte-exact compatibility and masked-value write-back risk.

options.title: Pause for reveal design
options.body: Hold the PR until default redaction, explicit raw reveal authorization, and marker semantics are designed together.

recommendation.title: Redact with explicit signal
recommendation.body: Keep default redaction, add stable structured metadata plus a text warning, and defer any privileged raw reveal path to separate reviewed work.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared redaction implementation and detection policy this PR relies on came from amknight's merged work, making them the strongest available history-based owner for the boundary decision.
